$comment: The phone-to-device protocol, shared between the firmware (C++, src/ble/) and the
bridge (TypeScript, bridge/src/protocol/). docs/bridge-protocol.md is normative and
client-independent; these vectors are what makes 'both sides implement the same
document' checkable rather than hoped for.
Authored by hand from the specification. Not generated from either implementation --
a generator would bake one side's mistakes into the vectors and the cross-check would
prove nothing. Every vector carries the field breakdown it was built from, so it can
be audited against the spec by reading.

groups.layout: byte 0: F(0x80) | L(0x40) | msgId(0x3F) | byte 1: chunkIndex | byte 2..: fragment
groups.fragmentBytes: MTU - 3 - 2, i.e. the ATT header and the two-byte chunk header

cases.note: A GET_INFO command at the negotiated MTU. Both F and L set, chunkIndex 0 -- the single-chunk form from 1.1.
SEND_TEXT at the 23-byte minimum MTU, which leaves 18 bytes per fragment. Three chunks: F on the first, L on the last, neither on the middle one.

vectors.name: chunk_three_c1
vectors.note: flags 0x09 = msgId 9, neither first nor last

groups.layout: byte 0: opcode | byte 1: txnId | byte 2..: body

vectors.name: rsp_err_not_authorised
vectors.note: PROVISION_KEY attempted on an unbonded connection. RSP_ERR echoes the txnId and names the opcode that failed. Section 2: it must not silently no-op -- that is how a network key ends up settable by anyone in Bluetooth range.

vectors.name: evt_budget
vectors.note: EVT_BUDGET. txnId 0 because events are unsolicited (1.2). limitMs 360000 is the g3 allowance from CLAUDE.md 1.3; nextTxUnix is what the UI turns into 'queued until HH:MM'.

vectors.name: evt_frame_tx_result
vectors.note: result 1 = undelivered after 4 attempts. Section 4: state 2 (queued) may later be followed by 0 or 1 for the same counter, so both the phone and the server treat the journal as a log of state transitions, not a set of final outcomes.

vectors.name: evt_journal_wrapping_tx_result
vectors.note: EVT_JOURNAL (D15). The same EVT_FRAME_TX_RESULT body as above, delivered out of the journal in answer to GET_QUEUE and therefore wrapped in its journal counter. The two counters are deliberately different: 4098 identifies the journal ENTRY, 1024 the FRAME it reports on. D10 turns on exactly that distinction, and a decoder that reads the frame counter as the journal counter passes every other vector in this file.

vectors.name: evt_journal_unknown_opcode
vectors.note: EVT_JOURNAL wrapping an event code no client knows. Section 4 requires it to be STORED and counted towards ACK_QUEUE anyway: the counter is legible even when the body is not, and dropping the entry would free journal space for something nobody ever saw. This is the vector that makes a future event type safe to add.

vectors.name: set_config_body
vectors.note: A SET_CONFIG body: configVersion u32 followed by a TLV run. The trailing 0xF0 is deliberately not a defined type -- section 3 requires unknown types to be ignored and reported back as unapplied, never to fail the whole write.

vectors.name: set_config_tlv_run
vectors.note: the same TLV run without the leading configVersion, for decoders tested in isolation
